reasons: Deviation classification is correct: Article IV fixes a 36-month Initial Period and grants only Licensor termination rights (immediate on any Licensee breach); there is no Customer convenience exit, which the rule expressly treats as walk-away/deviation for terms over 12 months, so neither the preferred nor the fallback position is met.

The redline is minimal and correctly directed: it inserts a new clause IV giving Licensee a 30-day convenience termination with refund of prepaid fees, tracking the model language, without disturbing existing text. No Licensor convenience right exists to delete (its immediate termination right is for-cause), so no further operation was required for rule completeness.

The failed deterministic check ('Customer convenience termination present') is a phrasing artifact — the inserted language uses the contract's defined term 'Licensee' rather than 'Customer' — and does not undermine substance.
Comment is accurate, concise, in the required voice, cites the playbook position and offers the 60-day fallback; severity 'high' matches the rule.
